text: Napoleon was short. You’ve heard it so many times, it just feels true.
He wasn’t. About 5′6″, or 7. Average for his time.
“Tiny Napoleon” came from British cartoons, and a mix-up between French and English inches.
So why did you believe it? Because you’d heard it before.
In 1977, psychologists found that simply repeating a statement makes people rate it as more true.
It’s called the illusory truth effect. Your brain mistakes familiar for true.
In 2015, researchers showed that even knowing the right answer doesn’t fully protect you.
Advertisers know this. Politicians know this. Your group chat runs on it.
Quick test. Is the Great Wall of China visible from space with the naked eye?
Feels like yes, right? NASA says it’s generally not. You’ve just heard it 100 times.
So next time something feels obviously true, ask: is it true, or just familiar?
